patch:
diff --git a/outbound/promo_sms.py b/outbound/promo_sms.py
new file mode 100644
index 0000000..ac04d57
--- /dev/null
+++ b/outbound/promo_sms.py
@@ -0,0 +1,10 @@
+"""The Tuesday promotional SMS."""
+
+
+def audience(contacts):
+    out = []
+    for contact in contacts:
+        if not contact.phone:
+            continue
+        out.append(contact.id)
+    return out

diff --git a/outbound/winback.py b/outbound/winback.py
new file mode 100644
index 0000000..aa5ff77
--- /dev/null
+++ b/outbound/winback.py
@@ -0,0 +1,12 @@
+"""The win-back campaign — lapsed contacts only."""
+
+
+def audience(contacts):
+    out = []
+    for contact in contacts:
+        if contact.segment != "lapsed":
+            continue
+        if not contact.email:
+            continue
+        out.append(contact.id)
+    return out
prompt:
Bo (c-02) set do-not-contact in June and got a win-back email from us last
Thursday. That is the second complaint this month and the policy in
`docs/contact_policy.md` is not ambiguous about what the flag means.

Make the outbound plan obey it. `python run.py` has to complete and every
audience count in it must be the count the policy gives.

Do not change `data/contacts.json`, and do not change the report's line shapes —
the send scheduler parses them.
title: do-not-contact is checked on one marketing channel of four
